6º de Primaria · Inglés

Modal verbs: can, must, should

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Tres frases: «Puedo nadar», «Debes llevar casco» y «Deberías beber agua». ¿Qué diferencia hay entre «debes» y «deberías»?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

«Debes» es una obligación (una norma): en inglés, You must wear a helmet. «Deberías» es un consejo: You should drink water. Y «puedo» es una capacidad: I can swim. Los tres son verbos modales.

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

What are modal verbs?

Modal verbs are special verbs that go before another verb to add a meaning: ability, permission, obligation or advice. The most common are can, must and should.

They have three golden rules: 1) the same form for all persons: «he can», not «he cans»; 2) the next verb has no to: «I can swim», not «I can to swim»; 3) no do/does in negatives and questions: «I can't», «Can you…?». En castellano: son como «poder» y «deber», pero sin conjugar.

Can: ability

We use can to talk about ability (capacidad, saber hacer algo): «I can ride a bike», «My sister can speak three languages», «Penguins can't fly, but they can swim very well».

For the past we use could / couldn't: «When I was five I could swim, but I couldn't read». Questions and short answers: «Can you play the guitar?» – «Yes, I can. / No, I can't». En castellano: «can» traduce «sé» o «puedo»: «I can swim» = «sé nadar».

Can: permission and requests

We also use can to ask for and give permission (permiso): «Can I go to the toilet, please?» – «Yes, you can». «You can't use your phone in class». And to make requests (pedir cosas): «Can you help me, please?».

A more polite way is could: «Could I open the window?», «Could you pass me the salt, please?». Consejo: en clase, pedir las cosas con Can I…, please? o Could I…? es muy educado.

Must and mustn't: rules

We use must for obligation and strong rules: «You must wear a seat belt», «Students must be on time». We use mustn't (must not) for prohibition (prohibido): «You mustn't run in the corridor», «You mustn't feed the animals».

Careful: mustn't means «it is forbidden», not «it isn't necessary». En castellano: «you must» = «debes / tienes que»; «you mustn't» = «no debes / está prohibido».

Vídeo: Must / mustn't: school rules · PUPPI Channel (YouTube) · 363 mil visualizaciones

Have to and don't have to

Have to also means obligation, often rules from other people: «I have to do my homework every day», «She has to wear a uniform». It changes with the person (has to) and uses do/does: «Do you have to get up early?».

Don't have to means it is not necessary: «Tomorrow is Saturday, so I don't have to go to school». Compare: «You mustn't touch it» (prohibido) and «You don't have to come» (no hace falta). En castellano: «no tienes que» no es lo mismo que «no debes».

Should: advice

We use should to give advice (consejos) and say what is a good idea: «You should go to bed early», «You look tired. You should rest». Shouldn't says it's a bad idea: «You shouldn't eat so many sweets».

To ask for advice: «What should I do?», «Should I tell the teacher?». En castellano: «should» es «deberías». Es más suave que must: no es una norma, es una recomendación.

Choosing the right modal

Ask yourself: is it an ability? → can. Is it permission? → can / could. Is it a rule or obligation? → must / have to. Is it forbidden? → mustn't. Is it advice? → should.

Examples: «You must stop at a red light» (rule). «You should wear a coat, it's cold» (advice). «I can touch my toes» (ability). «You mustn't use the lift in a fire» (forbidden).

Reading: rules at the swimming pool

Read the poster: «SWIMMING POOL RULES. You must have a shower before you swim. You must wear a swimming cap. You mustn't run around the pool. You mustn't eat in the water. Children under eight must be with an adult. You can use the slide from 11 to 1. Advice: you should wear flip-flops and you should drink water after swimming.»

Find two obligations, two prohibitions, one permission and one piece of advice.

Let's practise: class rules and advice

In groups, write the rules for your classroom: «We must listen when someone is speaking», «We mustn't shout», «We can read a book when we finish». Make a poster.

Then play «Problem and advice»: one student says a problem and the others give advice. «I can't sleep.» – «You should read a book», «You shouldn't use your tablet at night». Consejo: recuerda la regla de oro: después de un modal, el verbo va sin to y sin -s.

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Complete: «Dogs ___ climb trees.» (ability, negative)

  1. Capacidad → can.
  2. Negativa → can't.

Resultado: Dogs can't climb trees.

Ejemplo 2. Give advice: «I'm hungry.»

  1. Consejo → should + verbo.
  2. Sin to.

Resultado: You should eat a sandwich.

Ejemplo 3. Choose: «You (mustn't / don't have to) cross the road when the light is red.»

  1. Es una prohibición, no algo opcional.

Resultado: You mustn't cross the road when the light is red.

Errores típicos

  • Poner to tras el modal: «I can to swim» → «I can swim».
  • Poner -s: «she cans», «he musts» → «she can», «he must».
  • Usar do con modales: «Do you can…?» → «Can you…?».
  • Confundir mustn't (prohibido) con don't have to (no hace falta).
  • Usar must para un simple consejo: «You must try this cake» (mejor «You should try»).

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Write two things you can do and one you can't.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I can swim. I can draw. I can't play the piano.

  2. Make a question: «You can speak French.»

    Ver solución
    Can you speak French?

  3. Past: «I can read.» (when I was six)

    Ver solución
    I could read when I was six.

  4. Ask for permission to go out.

    Ver solución
    Can I go out, please? / Could I go out, please?

  5. Complete: «You ___ smoke in hospitals.»

    Ver solución
    mustn't.

  6. Complete: «It's Sunday. I ___ get up early.» (no hace falta)

    Ver solución
    don't have to.

  7. Give advice: «I've got a headache.»

    Ver solución
    You should rest / You should take a break.

  8. Correct: «She musts do her homework.»

    Ver solución
    She must do her homework.

  9. Translate: «No deberías ver tanta tele.»

    Ver solución
    You shouldn't watch so much TV.

  10. Write three rules for a library.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: You must be quiet. You mustn't eat. You can borrow three books.

Para familias

  • Escribid en inglés tres normas de casa con must / mustn't y pegadlas en la nevera.
  • Jugad a «problema y consejo»: uno cuenta un problema y el otro responde con should.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Expresión de capacidad, permiso, obligación, prohibición y consejo; verbos modales (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Cartel de normas de clase en inglés.
  • Juego «problema y consejo» por parejas.
  • Encuesta de habilidades «Can you…?» con gráfico.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use can and can't for ability, permission and possibility
  • Use must and mustn't for rules and obligation
  • Use should and shouldn't to give advice (consejos)
  • Remember the grammar of modal verbs: no -s, no to, no do
